newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MARCH 3-DEC 31, 1997.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MARCH 3-DEC 31, 1997.

text.p: (page 1/10 - March 3-9)
HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - Dutch presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (December 12-13).
MONDAY, MARCH 3
BRUSSELS - Environment Council (To March 4).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Community strategy on climate change.
- Convention on Biological Diversity:
- Biosafety Protocol.
- Future strategy for the control of atmospheric emissions from road transport taking into account the results of the auto-oil programme.
a) Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and amending Council directive 93/12/EEC;
b) Proposal for an EP and Council directive on measures to be taken against air pollution by emissions from motor vehicles and amending Council directives 70/156/EEC and 70/220/EEC.
- Communication on implementing Community environmental law.
- Preparation for the 5th session of the Commission on Sustainable Development and the special session of the General Assembly of the United Nations.
- Communication from the Commission to the Council and the EP on agreements in the environmental field.
- Proposal for a Council directive on the limitation of VOCs emissions.
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council framework directive on water.
- Humane trapping standards.
- Proposal for a Council decision on a Community action programme promoting non-governmental organisations primarily active in the field of environmental protection.
- Structured dialogue with the Central and East European Countries.
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0900 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Socialists hold conference on "Women's rights" (1000/0900 GMT). Main discussions focus on equal access to money and power; the inter-governmental conference (IGC) on EU reform; violence against women. Speakers include: European Commissioner Gradin. Venue: EP, Espace Leopold Building.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Scotland Europa hosts launch of "European regions' education network (EREN)" (0930/0830 GMT) (To March 4). Venue: Espace Messelle, 40 rue des Drapiers. Contact: Scotland Europa (322) 502 5028.
BRUSSELS - The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) holds conference on the environmental, technological and economic aspects of copper recycling (To March 4).
MOSCOW - EU and Russia hold summit; Commission President Santer, Commissioner van den Broek, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo attend.
TUESDAY, MARCH 4
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen meets U.S. permanent representative to NATO and members of the U.S. mission to the Alliance.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Women's Lobby holds press reception for the launch of the centre on violence against women (1500/1400 GMT). Venue: European Women's Lobby, 22 rue du Meridien. Contact: European Women's Lobby (322) 217 9020.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Information Technology Observatory (EITO) holds news conference (1100/1000 GMT). Discussions focus on the latest statistics and forecasts about the European market for information technology hardware and software, including communications technology; current and future technological trends and standards; the future of the Internet; electronic commerce over the Internet. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: EITO (32) 69 6603 1530.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 5
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - ECOSOC holds hearing on an update and review of the single market (1000/0900 GMT). Venue: ECOSOC. Contact: ECOSOC (322) 546 9207.

BRUSSELS - Club de Bruxelles holds conference on "Environment in Europe - The new strategy for waste management - Improving air quality - The new policy on noise pollution" (0915/0815 GMT) (To March 7). Speakers include: MEP Ken Collins. Venue: Management Centre Europe, 118 rue de L'Aqueduc. Contact: Club de Bruxelles (322) 743 1520.
THURSDAY, MARCH 6
BRUSSELS - Telecoms Council.
Provisional agenda includes:

- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the application of open network provision (ONP) to voice telephony and on universal service for telecommunications in a competitive environment (replacing EP and Council directive 95/62/EC).
- Proposal for a Council decision on the definition and implementation of Community policy in the field of telecommunications and postal services.
- (possibly) Action Plan from the Commission on satellite personal communications services.
- (possibly) Action Plan from the Commission on the potential health risks linked with mobile communications.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Conference Board Europe and American Electronics Association Europe hold joint conference on "The information society and electronic commerce". Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: Stephanie Holmgren, AEA Europe (322) 502 6734.

PARIS - CICERO Foundation holds conference on "Results of the IGC - preparing the Amsterdam treaty". Agenda includes: the issue of flexibility - will Britain block "Core Europe"?; is the Dutch presidency preparing a special strategy?; reforming the Common Foreign and Security Policy - the chances for a Mr CFSP; a breakthrough in the third pillar (justice and home affairs); institutional arrangements - power struggle or compromise?; the IGC seen from Central and Eastern Europe. Contact: CICERO Foundation (33) 1 42 67 9204.
WARSAW - CER, UIC and UNIFE hold joint conference on "The pan-European dimension of rail transport" (0900/0800 GMT). Contact: Rita Moosen, CER (322) 525 9079.

WELS-UPPER, Austria - Energiesparverband, in cooperation with the European Commission, holds conference on "World energy efficiency day" (0800/0700 GMT). Discussions focus on energy efficiency-the gateway to our future; local and regional strategies for energy efficiency; energy efficiency in industry. Venue: City Hall. Contact: Energiesparverband (43) 732 6584 4380.
FRIDAY, MARCH 7
BRUSSELS - European Commission sponsors conference on priority actions for completion of the single market.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European disability forum - Founding general assembly (0900/0800 GMT) (To March 8). Speakers include: MEPs Barbara Schmidbauer, Richard Howitt, Bartho Pronk. Venue: Vlaams Europees Conferentie Centrum, 1-3 rue du Marquis.
SATURDAY, MARCH 8

LUXEMBOURG - Forex Luxembourg celebrates its 40th anniversary. European Commission President Santer and Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker attend. Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 2/10 - March 10-17)
MONDAY, MARCH 10
BRUSSELS - Internal Market Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Impact and effectiveness of the internal market.
- Legislative simplification.

- White paper on approximation of the laws of the Central and Eastern European Countries in the field of the internal market - Preparation for the meeting with the Central and Eastern European Countries.
- (possibly) Proposal for a directive on pluralism and concentration in the media.
- European Company Statute.

- Proposal for a Council decision with a view to accession by the European Community to the Revised 1958 agreement on the adoption of uniform conditions of approval and reciprocal recognition of approval for motor vehicle equipment and parts.
- Proposal for a Council decision on the conclusion of an agreement on customs cooperation and mutual assistance between the Community and Canada.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States relating to pressure equipment.
- (possibly) Proposal for an EP and Council directive on certain components and characteristics of two-or three-wheel motor vehicles.

- (possibly) Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 93/116/EEC to facilitate the free movement of doctors and the mutual recognition of their diplomas, certificates and other evidence of formal qualifications.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending the Council Directives on the maximum design speed of wheeled agricultural or forestry tractors.

- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 89/398/EEC on the approximation of the laws of the Member States on foodstuffs intended for particular nutritional uses ("dietary foodstuffs").
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 9512/EC on food additives other than colours and sweeteners.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To March 14).
TUESDAY, MARCH 11
BRUSSELS - Transport Council (To March 12).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Air Transport:

- Proposal for a Council directive amending Council directive 92/14/EEC on the limitation of the operation of aeroplanes covered by Part II, Chapter 2, volume I of Annex 16 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, second edition (1988).
- Levies on aircraft fuel.
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council directive establishing safety assessment of aircraft from third countries using Community airports.

- (possibly) Draft recommendation for a Council decision authorising the Commission to start negotiations with a view to establishing Community membership of the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation (Eurocontrol).
- (possibly) Draft recommendation for a Council decision authorising the Commission to start negotiations with a view to establishing a European organisation responsible for civil aviation safety.
- Inland Transport:
- Proposal for a Council directive on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures.
- Proposal for a Council regulation concerning the granting of Community financial assistance for actions to promote combined goods transport (PACT).
- Proposal for a Council Regulation amending Council regulation (EEC) No 3821/85 and Council directive 88/599/EEC on recording equipment in road transport.
- (possibly) Interoperability of road pricing and Intelligent Transport Systems.
- Other Measures:
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on summertime arrangements.
- (possibly) Community action programme on road safety.
- (possbly) Negotiations between the European Community and Switzerland.

BRUSSELS - Inernational Accounting Standards Committee holds conference on "International accounting standards - Implications for major European corporations" (1000/0900 GMT) (To March 12). Venue: Sheraton Hotel. Contact: Clare McSheaffrey, Touchstone Exhibitions and Conferences (44) 181 332 0044.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 12
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (To March 13).
THURSDAY, MARCH 13

METZ, France - Lorraine Regional Council, under the patronage of the European Commission, holds second European colloquium on "SMEs" (0830/0730 GMT). Topics include: third multiannual programme for SMEs; the euro: regulations and stakes for the single currency. Venue: Espace Saarlorlux. Contact: French EU Representation (322) 229 8461.

AMSTERDAM - Second official ECR Europe - Efficient consumer conference (1000/0900 GMT) (To March 14). Topics include: joining forces - new mindsets for new relationships; the new reality of the supply chain; anticipating and responding to new consumer demand. Venue: Amsterdam RAI, International exhibition and congress centre. Contact: CIES (33) 1 44 34 69 06.
FRIDAY, MARCH 14
ROTTERDAM - Informal Social Affairs Council (To March 15). No agenda yet available.
LUXEMBOURG - Benelux Consultative Interparliamentary Council holds conference on the euro (1000/0900 GMT) (To March 15). Speakers include: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker.
SATURDAY, MARCH 15

APELDOORN, Netherland (EXPANDED ITEM) - Informal General Affairs Council (1300/1200 GMT) (To March 16). Discussions on how to proceed with negotiations with 10 former communist bloc countries that have been promised eventual EU membership.
SUNDAY, MARCH 16
APELDOORN, Netherland (NEW ITEM) - Informal General Affairs Council (1000/0900 GMT). Discussion on Turkey and Cyprus.
MONDAY, MARCH 17
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "The governance in the Euro-Mediterranean region" (To March 18).
BRUSSELS - ECOFIN Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Preparation of stage 3 of EMU.

- Annual report of the Court of Auditors and discharge - report by the Court of Auditors for 1995 and discharge - Court of Auditors statement of assurance for 1995 - Commission report on the follow-up of recommendations during the 1994 procedure.
- Economic situation in the EU.
- (possibly) Financial assistance to third countries.
BRUSSELS - Farm Council (To March 19). No agenda yet available. Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 3/10 - Mar 18-Apr 10)
TUESDAY, MARCH 18

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Management Global Information (MGI) holds conference on "Monetary Union and large firms - How to manage the euro project" (0900/0800 GMT) (To March 19). Discussions include: how to take into account the changeover to the euro both in business processes and information systems; key opportunities for corporate finance and treasury departments linked to the switchover to the euro. Venue: Hotel Le Meridien. Contact: MGI (33) 1 41 10 20 80.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Business Aviation Association (EBAA) holds conference on "An uplift for business aviation" (1100/1000 GMT) (To March 20). Venue: Sodehotel. Contact: EBAA (322) 721 4272.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 19
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To March 20).
THURSDAY, MARCH 20

BRUSSELS - Euromanagement holds conference on "Industrial water management" (To March 21). The conference aims to help industry improve its water and wastewater management. Contact: Gabrielle Smit, Euromanagement (31) 40 297 4944.
FRIDAY MARCH 21
TOULOUSE, France - Institut Superieur de Recherche pour l'Europe holds seminar on "The inter-governmental conference (IGC)". Contact: Institut Superieur de Recherche pour l'Europe (33) 5 61 52 7375.
MONDAY, MARCH 24
BRUSSELS - General Affairs Council (To March 25).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Former Yugoslavia.
- Former Yugolav Republic of Macedonia (FYROM): decision to sign a cooperation agreement.
- Albania: adoption of negotiating directives for a cooperation agreement.
- Middle East peace process.
- Relations with Turkey: preparation of Association Council.
- Pakistan: state of negotiations on a trade and cooperation agreement.
- Trade questions, including - Conclusion of an Information Technology Agreement.
- Relations with South Africa:
- State of negotiations on a cooperation agreement;
- Protocol of accession to the Lome Convention.
- Preparation of 23rd ACP-EC Council of Ministers (24-25 April 1997) (possible A point).
- Relations with Australia.
- Mediterranean policy:
- Preparation of 2nd Ministerial meeting (Barcelona process) (15-16 April 1997);
- State of negotiations with Egypt, Lebanon, Jordan and Algeria.
- European Monitoring Centre on racism and xenophobia.
- Transatlantic relations.
- Russia: decision to conclude the Partnership and Cooperation Agreement.
- Baltic States: Europe agreements.
- Association Council with Romania: determination of the Union's position.
- Preparation of the structured dialogue meeting with the Central and Eastern European Countries.
- VII Ministerial meeting EU-Rio Group: determination of the Union's position.
- In the margins of the Council:
- Association Council with Romania;
- Structured dialogue meeting with the CEEC;
- Signature of the cooperation agreement with FYROM.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds debate on "EU competition policy - Third party rights - Use or abuse?" (1730/1630 GMT). Venue: Meridien Hotel. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium (322) 540 9030.
TUESDAY, MARCH 25
ROME (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers hold special conclave to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 1957 Treaty of Rome.
Agenda includes:
- (1000/0900 GMT) The state of the inter-governmental conference (IGC).
- (1300/1200 GMT) Prime Minister Romano Prodi and European Commission President Santer hold joint news conference on the outcome of the General Affairs Council meeting.
- (1345/1245 GMT) Lunch hosted by Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
- (1600/1500 GMT) Official commemoration ceremony of the 40th anniversary of the 1957 Treaty of Rome.
- (1700/1600 GMT) EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo and European Commission President Santer hold joint news conference following the ceremony.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Commission meeting.
- (1730/1630 GMT) National parliament presidents meet.
- (2000/1900 GMT) Rome mayor hosts reception.
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0900 GMT).
FRIDAY, MARCH 28
- EU institutions closed for Easter holidays to March 31 inclusive.
APRIL
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Bosnian donor countries hold conference to discuss future of former Yugoslavia.
FRIDAY, APRIL 4
NOORDWIJK, Netherlands - Informal ECOFIN Council (To April 6). Possible decision on the selection of the winning design for the euro coins, on the basis of a report of a jury that is to be installed.
SUNDAY, APRIL 6
MAASTRICHT - Informal Cultural Affairs Council (To April 8). No agenda yet available.
MONDAY, APRIL 7
NOORDWIJK - EU-Rio Group meeting involving South American countries and Mexico, Panama, Trinidad, Tobago and Costa Rica (To April 8).
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To April 11).

BONN (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts first annual electronic commerce conference "G7 - Global marketplace for SMEs project" (To April 9). Contact: Sandra Helms, Empirica GmbH (49) 228 985 3888.
BERLIN - International European Training Centre holds seminar on "Building Europe: EU enlargement and deepening". Contact: International European Training Centre (33) 4 92 15 2121.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts ministerial conference on social integration (To April 11).
THURSDAY, APRIL 10
LUXEMBOURG - Consumers Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Voluntary agreements as important instruments for consumer policy - Council resolution.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on injunctions for the protection of consumer interests.

- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 87/102/EEC (as amended by Directive 90/88/EEC) for the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning consumer credit.
- (possibly) Report of the Commission on the application of directive 87/012/EEC concerning consumer credit.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the sale of consumer goods and associated guarantees. Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 4/10 - Apr 11-29)
FRIDAY, APRIL 11

LONDON - The Royal Institute of International Affairs holds conference on "Trade and environment: conflict or compatibility?". Sessions include: trade and environment after Singapore; trade versus environment - the evidence; industry concerns; resolving trade and environment disputes; the future. Speakers include: European Commissioner Brittan. Venue: Chatham House, 10 St James Square. Contact: Sharon Moore (44) 171 957 5700.
MONDAY, APRIL 14
LUXEMBOURG - Fisheries Council (To April 15).
Provisional agenda includes:
- MAGPs IV, Council decision on Multiannual Guidance Programmes (Structural arrangements for 1997-1999).
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation laying down certain technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources.
- Proposal for a Council decision on a specific measure to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities.
- (possibly) Communication from the Commission to Council and EP on fisheries agreements (Present situation and future prospects).
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation allocating among Member States, for 1997, Community fish quotas of Atlanto-Scandian herring and horse mackerel.
- (possibly) Accession of Community to General Fisheries Council for the Mediterranean.
- (possibly) Consultations with Norway on a new management regime for North Sea herring.
- (possibly) Consultations with Norway on a new management regime for mackerel.
- Proposal for a Council regulation providing for the opening and management of autonomous Community tariff quotas for certain fisheries products (1997).
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 16
BRUSSELS - Aeronautica holds "European air transport conference" (To April 17). Venue: Sheraton Towers. Contact: Aeronautica (44) 181 893 3795.
THURSDAY, APRIL 17
LUXEMBOURG - Social Affairs Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Employment and Labour Market Committee.
- Modified proposal for a directive on "Chemical Agents".
- Worker information and consultation.
- (possibly) Commission activities of analysis, research, cooperation and action in the field of employment.
- (possibly) Directive modifying directive 90/394/CEE concerning the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
- (possibly) New communication on the future of social protection.
- (possibly) White Paper on working time in excluded sectors.
- Proposal for a directive: "Burden of proof in cases of discrimination based on sex".

- Proposal for a directive amending directive 76/207/EEC on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women as regards access to employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions (Kalanke Ruling).
- Collective redundancies (Codification).
- Council Recommendation on home working.
MAASTRICHT - Dutch EU presidency hosts post-Lome ministerial meeting (April 18).
FRIDAY, APRIL 18
AMSTERDAM - Informal Environment Council (To April 20). No agenda yet available.
MONDAY, APRIL 21
LUXEMBOURG - Farm Council (To April 22). No agenda yet available.

MALTA - European Documentation and Research Centre (EDRC) and University of Malta hold conference on "The State of the European Union Conference 1997". Main discussions on the development of EU policies especially with regard to the EU citizens' ombudsman; the evolution of cooperation in Justice and Home Affairs in Europe; EC social policy; EU initiatives for employment and growth and the EU SME Policy. Contact: Monica Cauchi, EDRC (356) 32 90 20 01.
TUESDAY, APRIL 22
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0900 GMT).
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 23
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To April 24).
BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (To April 24).
THURSDAY, APRIL 24
LUXEMBOURG - Industry Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Shipbuilding:
a) (possibly) Individual cases of state aid;
b) Future of Community policy on state aid in connection with the situation regarding ratifications of the OECD Aereement.
- Competitiveness of the European industry - Report by the Commission.
- State Aid:
- 5th Survey report on state aid by the Commission;
- State of affairs regarding proposals related to art. 94 of the Treaty.
- (possibly) Action programme in the field of the Information Society.
LUXEMBOURG - ACP-EU Council (To April 25). No agenda yet available.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Innovative research and appropriate health care for the people of Europe" (To April 25).
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Trafficking in women" (To April 26).
TUESDAY, APRIL 29
LUXEMBOURG - General Affairs Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Association Council with Poland: determination of the Union's position.
- Association Council with Hungary: determination of the Union's position.
- Former Yugoslavia.
- Middle East peace process.
- Mediterranean policy:
- Malta: Commission communication;
- State of negotiations with Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan;
- follow up to 2nd Ministerial meeting (Barcelona process).
- (possibly) Association Council with Turkey: determination of the Union's position.
- Relations with Switzerland.
- (possibly) Burma/Myanmar: extension of the common position.
- Zaire: support for the electoral process.
- Anti-personnel landmines.
- Transatlantic relations.
- Trade questions - OECD negotiations on a Multilateral Agreement on Investment: state of play.
- In the margins of the Council:
- Association Council with Poland;
- Association Council with Hungary;
- (possibly) Association Council with Turkey. Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 5/10 - May 1-20)
THURSDAY, MAY 1
- EU institutions closed for Labour Day.
THURSDAY, MAY 8
- EU institutions closed for Ascension holiday.
FRIDAY, MAY 9
- EU institutions closed for "Robert Schuman" remembrance day.
MONDAY, MAY 12
BRUSSELS - ECOFIN Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Preparation of stage 3 of EMU.
- Excessive deficit procedure:
- Assessment of excessive deficits (Article 104 c, paragraph 6);
- Abrogation of excessive deficits (Article 104 c, paragraph 12);
- Assessment of recommendations (Article 104 c, paragraph 7).
- (possibly) Follow-up to the informal meeting of ECOFIN Ministers (Noordwijk, 4-6 April 1997).
- (possibly) Employment.
- Taxation.
- Fight against fraud: transit sector.
BRUSSELS - Farm Council (To May 13). No agenda yet available.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To May 16).
WEDNESDAY, MAY 14
BRUSSELS - Research Council (To May 15).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Preparation for meeting with Central and Eastern European Ministers (Structured dialogue).
- (possibly) Financial supplement to the Fourth RTD Framework Programme.
- 5th RTD Framework Programme.
- First Action Programme on Innovation.
- International cooperation in the RTD field:
- S/T cooperation strategy with Mediterranean/Central and Eastern European Countries/emerging economies;
- Bilateral S/T agreements with certain third countries.
- Evaluation and monitoring of Community RTD activities.
- High Flux Reactor (HFR).
- Research and development cooperation.
- (possibly) Fusion Programme and ITER.
- (possibly) SPACE.
FLORENCE, Italy - European Natural Gas Vehicle Association (ENGVA) holds conference on "Creating the climate for NGVs" (To May 16). Contact: ENGVA (31) 20 597 3100.
THURSDAY, MAY 15
AMSTERDAM - Committee of the Regions holds first summit of the regions and cities. Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
SATURDAY, MAY 17

GENEVA - The International Telecommunications Union celebrates the world telecommunications day "Telecommunications and humanitarian assistance" commemorating its founding in Paris 132 years ago. Contact: International Telecommunications Union (41) 22 730 5111.
MONDAY, MAY 19
- EU institutions closed for Whit Monday holiday.
TUESDAY, MAY 20
BRUSSELS - Internal Market Council.
Provisional agenda includes:

- Legislative simplification.
- Amended proposal for a directive of the EP and of the Council on the legal protection of designs.
- (possibly) Proposal for a regulation on the Community design.

BRUSSELS - World Fuels Conferences holds conference on "Fuel quality and vehicle technology" (To May 22). Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: World Fuels Conferences (1) 703 812 0902.
SUNDAY, MAY 25
MIDDELBURG, Netherlands - Informal Farm Council (To May 27). No agenda yet available.
MONDAY, MAY 26

Provisional agenda includes:
